Karczew Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Karczew, Poland

Not demolished. Jews began settling in Karczew in the late 18th century; by 1921, 836 Jews made up over a quarter of the town's population, deported to the Warsaw Ghetto in January 1941 and mostly murdered at Treblinka in 1942. The cemetery likely dates to the late 18th or early 19th century. During the war, Germans carried out executions here, burying ghetto and forced-labor-camp victims; in 1948, roughly 200 people murdered in 1942 at the nearby Marpe sanatorium were exhumed and reburied at the site. The cemetery later became an illegal landfill and sand mine; 1980s pumping-station construction damaged part of the hill, displacing graves. A 2002 restoration, funded by the Jewish Community in Warsaw and several international partners, fenced and cleaned the site; around 2016, an ohel was erected for tzaddik Awraham Jehoszua Heszel, who died in 1914.
